Observed:
- Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below the left lower eyelid
- Focal, non-tender, indurated elevation along the inferior orbital rim
- Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and multinucleated giant cells on histopathology
- 69-year-old woman
- Several-month history of the lesion
- History of chronic scleritis treated with NSAIDs
- Left levator resection for ptosis
- Dacryocystorhinostomy one month before the onset of the lesion
- Two courses of antibiotics for presumed postoperative cellulitis
- Lesion persisted despite antibiotic treatment
- CT scan showed soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid
- No bony invasion or extension into surrounding structures
- Excisional biopsy performed
- Intraoperative frozen sections revealed granulomatous inflammation
- Final histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and multinucleated giant cells
- No evidence of malignancy
- Bacterial and fungal stains (Ziehl–Neelsen and Grocott) were negative
Differential diagnosis:
1. Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
2. Granuloma faciale
3. Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
4. Sarcoidosis
5. Periocular granuloma annulare
